title: Equivariant preparation and fixed-locus blowup charts
statement:
Let $f:(X,Z)\to(S,D)$ be a log smooth morphism of Noetherian fs log regular pairs [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], with $X$ regular and $Z$ a $G$-strict strict normal crossings divisor. $G$-strict means that distinct translates of any irreducible boundary component are disjoint. A log regular pair means its fs log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O^\times$ for the boundary complement $j$; strict normal crossings means locally a product of distinct regular parameters, with regular global components and regular intersections of the expected codimension. Let a finite group $G$ act tamely over $S$, trivially on $S$. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ and replace $G$ by its inertia group there. For any subgroup $H\le G$, etale locally near this point and its image there is a strict equivariant etale comparison from $X$ to the pullback over $S$ of
$$Y=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_t^{\pm1},z_1,\ldots,z_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]\longrightarrow\Sigma=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q].$$
Here $Q$ is a sharp fs chart of $S$, $\Lambda$ is a localization of $\mathbf Z[1/N,\mu_N]$ with $N$ invertible at the point, $N$ annihilates the inertia group, $\mu_N$ denotes the $N$th roots of unity, $P=\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$ is a chart for the boundary $T=(z_1\cdots z_r=0)$, and the map is induced by $\gamma:Q\to P$ with injective group completion and finite invertible torsion in its cokernel. The $u_j$ are fixed by inertia, each $z_j$ is an eigenvector, and the $y_j$ span a finite free inertia representation. Coordinates for the latter may be chosen after restriction to $H$ so that
$$Y^H=V(z_1,\ldots,z_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$$
for some $0\le m\le r$, $0\le n\le s$. If $H$ acts trivially, its fixed subscheme is the whole scheme and is omitted from the blowup procedure.

The blowup and the strict transform of the boundary commute with this comparison: for the model $X=S\times_\Sigma Y$, there are scheme isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Bl}_{X^H}X=X\times_Y\operatorname{Bl}_{Y^H}Y,\qquad Z^{\rm st}=X\times_YT^{\rm st}.$$
The same assertions hold after the strict etale comparison. Here the fixed subscheme is the equalizer of all elements of $H$, the blowup is $\operatorname{Proj}\bigoplus_{a\ge0}I^a$, and strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image away from the center. On the $z_i$ blowup chart ($1\le i\le m$), $z_j=z_i z'_j$ for $j\le m$, $j\ne i$, and $y_j=z_i y'_j$ for $j\le n$; all other variables are unchanged. For the boundary given by the union of the exceptional divisor and the strict transform of $T$, its chart monoid is $\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$, and the base map is $(1\oplus\beta_i)\gamma$ with $\beta_i(e_j)=e_j+e_i$ for $j\le m$, $j\ne i$, and all other basis vectors fixed. On the $y_i$ chart ($1\le i\le n$), $z_j=y_i z'_j$ for $j\le m$ and $y_j=y_i y'_j$ for $j\le n$, $j\ne i$. For the boundary given by the union of the exceptional divisor and the strict transform of $T$, its chart monoid is $\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^{r+1}$; the base map is $(1\oplus\delta)\gamma$ with $\delta(e_j)=e_j+e_{r+1}$ for $j\le m$ and $\delta(e_j)=e_j$ otherwise. In both cases the variables outside this monoid are polynomial variables; these charts cover the blowup.

source.place: X Proposition 1.2, 1.3, Lemmas 1.5--1.6 and 1.7, pp.136--146; specifically the claim in 1.7 and its Ui, Vi charts.

proof.text: The inertia group has invertible order by tameness; shrink at the image point so this order is invertible. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] to the base, whose group action is trivial. It gives a sharp chart $Q$ and the cyclotomic coefficient map; take $N=|G|$ and localize $\Lambda$ at the image point. The chart characters on the base are trivial because its sections are fixed. At $\bar x$, inertia preserves each boundary branch: a branch and any of its translates through this point intersect, and $G$-strictness forbids distinct such translates. Thus it acts trivially on the characteristic monoid. The regularity criterion [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] gives $\overline M_{X,\bar x}\cong\mathbf N^r$. The hypotheses of equivariant preparation are now all in force.

source.place: X 1.3, printed pp.139--140, reduction to inertia, sharp base chart and condition (vi).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-equivariant-log-smooth-chart] with this fixed base chart. Obtain the eigenvector chart $P$ and a strict smooth equivariant comparison. Localize $P$ at the face of elements whose images at $\bar x$ are units; this corresponds to an open neighborhood of the chart image, so the comparison remains smooth. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] the units of the localized monoid form the subgroup generated by the face, and the sharp quotient is fs and sharp; the chart identifies it with the characteristic monoid $\overline M_{X,\bar x}\cong\mathbf N^r$ of Step 1, since both are $P$ modulo the elements invertible at $\bar x$. The group completion, which localization does not change, is torsion free: if $nt=0$ with $n>0$ and $t\in P^{\rm gp}$, saturation of $P$ gives $t,-t\in P$, so $t\in P^\times$, and $P^\times$ is torsion free by [lem-per-equivariant-log-smooth-chart]; hence $t=0$. In particular the unit subgroup is torsion free and the sharp quotient has torsion-free group $\mathbf Z^r$. Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-splitting] to identify the localized $P$ with $\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$. Restrict the character homomorphism of the chart to these factors. The variables from $\mathbf N^r$ are the $z_j$. If $u$ is any monomial in $P^\times$, it is nonzero at $\bar x$. Since inertia fixes that geometric point and $g(u)=\chi(g,u)u$, its residue forces $\chi(g,u)=1$ in the residue field. Distinct $N$th roots of unity remain distinct when $N$ is invertible, so $\chi(g,u)=1$ in $\Lambda$. Thus all $u_j$ are fixed. Localization and these monoid isomorphisms preserve the injectivity and torsion condition of $\gamma^{\rm gp}$.

Use [lem-per-tame-smooth-representation-chart] on the smooth comparison to $S\times_\Sigma\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[P]$. It gives a free representation $V$ and an equivariant etale comparison $c:X\to S\times_\Sigma Y$. The added symmetric factor carries the trivial log structure, so $c$ remains strict. Fix $H\leq G$ and put $e=|H|^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}h$ on $V$. Directly $e^2=e$, $e(h-1)=0$, and $v-ev=|H|^{-1}\sum_h(v-hv)$. Hence $\ker e$ is exactly the submodule generated by the differences $(h-1)v$, and $V=\ker e\oplus\operatorname{im}e$, with $V_H\cong\operatorname{im}e$. Both summands are finite projective, being summands of finite free $V$, and are free by [lem-trf-projective-over-local-free] since $\Lambda$ was localized at a prime. Choose bases, calling the basis of $\ker e$ the first $n$ variables. The ideal of the fixed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Sym}V$ is therefore $(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$. For each $z_j$ a nontrivial restricted character yields a difference $(\chi(h)-1)z_j$ with unit coefficient in this localization; a trivial character yields no equation. Renumbering gives precisely $(z_1,\ldots,z_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ as the fixed ideal in $Y$. This uses coinvariants, not the invariant subring.

source.place: X 1.2 second assertion, printed p.138; 1.5(a)--(c), printed p.142; 1.7 choice of coordinates, printed p.144.

proof.text: The fixed-locus comparison is cartesian near $\bar x$. Indeed on $c^{-1}((S\times_\Sigma Y)^H)$ the maps $h$ and the identity have the same image under $c$. Their equalizer is open, since the diagonal of an etale morphism is open [def-weil-etale-morphism]. It contains $\bar x$. Intersect these finitely many opens (and their translates for the other subgroups) and shrink to obtain equality with the fixed subscheme. Because $H$ is trivial on $S$, fixed points commute with the pullback $S\times_\Sigma Y$ by the defining equalizer. Strictness similarly identifies $Z$ with the pullback of $T$. Hence it suffices to prove the asserted comparison for $X_0=S\times_\Sigma Y$, and then pull back along $c$.

source.place: X 1.4 opening and squares (1.a)--(1.c), printed p.141; 1.7 opening, printed p.143.

proof.text: Work first with $X_0=S\times_\Sigma Y$. In strict local rings over $\bar s$, apply [lem-per-log-regular-chart-monomial-tor] to the chart $Q\to P$ from Step 2. The fixed ideal is generated by some $z_j$ and $y_j$, so the node gives Tor independence of the square for $Y^H\hookrightarrow Y$. It also gives Tor independence for each coordinate intersection $T_J=V(z_j:j\in J)$ and for $Y^H\cap T_J$, since these add only monomial generators and kill the same subset of polynomial variables. The assertions are local, so these strict-local vanishings give the required Tor-independent squares on a neighborhood. The fixed subscheme and these intersections are coordinate subspaces in a polynomial/Laurent polynomial ring: their ideals are generated by the indicated distinct variables, which are regular sequences by successive polynomial expansion. The immersion $Y^H\cap T_J\hookrightarrow T_J$ is given by the remaining distinct variables (the zero ideal is allowed). Apply [lem-per-tor-independent-blowup-transform], first to the center and then to the boundary components and their intersections. Its hypotheses include the regularity of $Y$ (a polynomial/Laurent polynomial scheme over the localized cyclotomic field or discrete valuation ring), regularity of $X_0$ near the comparison point (it is etale locally the regular $X$), and the normal crossings property of both boundaries. It yields both displayed scheme isomorphisms for the blowup and for the strict transform of the entire boundary. In particular no flatness of $X_0\to Y$ has been assumed.

source.place: X Lemmas 1.5--1.6, printed pp.141--143; 1.7 Claim and proof, printed p.144.

proof.text: The same regular-center comparison applies to the etale map $c$, which is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; all its Tor-independent squares are consequently available. Thus the blowup and strict-transform isomorphisms in Step 5 pull back to the original etale neighborhood. For $m+n=0$ the fixed subscheme is all of $Y$, and we omit that operation, as required. For $m+n>0$, let $R=\Lambda[u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_t^{\pm1},z_1,\ldots,z_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]$. The regular-sequence presentation [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] identifies the chart for each generator $a$ of $I=(z_1,\ldots,z_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ with $R[w_b:b\ne a]/(aw_b-b)$. Eliminating the original variables $b$ gives the polynomial rings in the statement; the substitution sends $b$ to $aw_b$ and fixes all other coordinates, and its inverse sends $w_b$ to $b/a$. The generator charts cover by [lemma-nagata-rees-generators-cover-proj].

source.place: X 1.7, printed pp.144--145, the Ui and Vi affine charts; Stacks Tag 0BIQ (regular-sequence chart presentation).

proof.text: On the $z_i$ chart, the exceptional equation is $z_i=0$. The strict transform of the component $z_i=0$ is empty, because outside the center its inverse image misses this chart. For $j\leq m$, $j\ne i$, the total equation is $z_i z'_j$, and saturation by powers of $z_i$ leaves $z'_j$; for $j>m$ the strict equation remains $z_j$. These saturations follow by writing a polynomial as a sum of monomials: multiplication by $z_i$ is injective modulo each of these coordinate ideals. Thus the union of the exceptional divisor and the strict transform has exactly the $r$ distinct boundary coordinates $(z'_1,\ldots,z'_{i-1},z_i,z'_{i+1},\ldots,z'_m,z_{m+1},\ldots,z_r)$. The other coordinates are polynomial directions, and the invertible $u_j$ give the $\mathbf Z^t$ factor. For $j\leq m$, $j\ne i$, substitution in the monomial $z_j$ multiplies the new $j$th monomial by $z_i$, hence $e_j\mapsto e_j+e_i$; all other $e_j$ are fixed. Consequently the base chart map is $(1\oplus\beta_i)\gamma$.

source.place: X 1.7(a), printed p.145, boundary, decomposition and beta.

proof.text: On the $y_i$ chart, the exceptional equation is $y_i=0$. Every boundary component has strict equation $z'_j=0$ for $j\leq m$ and $z_j=0$ for $j>m$, since its total equation is respectively $y_i z'_j$ or $z_j$ and saturation by $y_i$ removes exactly the factor $y_i$. Again this is checked by polynomial expansion modulo the coordinate ideals. Adjoining the exceptional coordinate to these $r$ boundary coordinates gives $\mathbf N^{r+1}$, together with the same $\mathbf Z^t$ unit factor; the remaining $y'_j$ and $y_j$ are polynomial directions. The substitution $z_j=y_i z'_j$ gives $e_j\mapsto e_j+e_{r+1}$ for $j\leq m$, with $e_j$ fixed otherwise, so the base chart map is $(1\oplus\delta)\gamma$. These computations also cover $m=0$, $n=0$, $r=0$ and a single-generator center whenever the corresponding chart exists.

source.place: X 1.7(b), printed pp.145--146, boundary, decomposition and beta (called delta here).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q143-207ada543 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes and every cited statement in full, against ILO X 1.1–1.7, printed pp.135–146. That covers 1.2 with equations (1)–(5) and the P0 paragraph, 1.3 (i)–(vii) and (1.d), Lemmas 1.5–1.6, the 1.7 Claim, the U_i/V_i charts and the β/δ monoid maps. The statement matches the base apart from three clarifications: G-strict is defined, strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure, and the new boundary is exceptional divisor ∪ strict transform. Allowing m = 0 is a harmless generalisation, handled by the V_i charts. Step 1: tame inertia has invertible order; the base action is trivial; G-strictness plus unibranch SNC components means inertia fixes every branch; VI 1.4 gives M̄ ≅ N^r; all hypotheses of the equivariant-chart node hold. Step 2 is the repaired fault: it asserted with no reason that the face units F^gp are torsion free. The fix shows P^gp is torsion free because P is saturated and P^× is torsion free, then applies the unit splitting. The residue-field argument for trivial unit characters is correct. Step 3: idempotent, coinvariants, free summands over local Λ, ζ^a − 1 a unit; I checked the fixed ideal. Step 4: the equaliser is open via the étale diagonal; the fixed locus commutes with S×_Σ. Step 5: monomial Tor applied to Y^H, T_J and Y^H∩T_J; strict-local vanishing spreads by faithfully flat descent and coherence; the hypotheses of the blowup node hold. Step 6 uses 0BIQ and the Rees cover. Steps 7–8: I checked the saturations and tested Z/2 acting on A² by −1, plus the cases m = 0 and a single generator. New nodes are all true and statement-only. The equivariant chart is X 1.2 (Z/2 on A¹ tested); it is not the non-equivariant Q50 Kato chart. The tame Sym V chart holds by averaging a lift through the Jacobian criterion; ILO's radicial base change is not needed. The monomial-Tor node I proved through the complete-local model (flat in equal characteristic; g a nonzerodivisor via the associated graded in mixed characteristic). It generalises lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart, which covers only Tor_1 and P = Q, so it is not a duplicate. The Tor-independent blowup node is X 1.6, with ILO's typo of V for W corrected; its NCD paragraph holds by Mayer–Vietoris. None of the new nodes restates a clause of the item, and there is no cycle and no SGA. Tool uses accepted: three trf monoid lemmas, 0593, 0BIQ, Nagata Rees cover and étale def. Batch-5: def-trf-fs-log-blowup and def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale are general definitions. lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary is VI 1.4 log-regular local algebra; its closure of 1040 nodes contains no thm-trf, trace transport, Poincaré-duality node or batch-4 target. fs-face-sharpening, fine-monoid-unit-splitting, projective-over-local-free and blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation are pure algebra. All flags accepted; none is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality.
